questions.question: True or false: Bruriah was the daughter of Rabbi Hananiah ben Teradion and the wife of Rabbi Meir.
questions.explanation: Her father was one of the Ten Martyrs of the Kingdom, and her husband was one of the foremost disciples of Rabbi Akiva.

questions.question: True or false: Rabbi Hananiah ben Teradion taught Torah to both his son and his daughter.
questions.explanation: This was an exceptional step for his time, and in the scholarly competition between the siblings Bruriah stood out.

questions.question: How was her father, Rabbi Hananiah ben Teradion, executed?
options: By burning, wrapped in a Torah scroll
questions.explanation: He was caught teaching Torah in public in the days of the decrees of religious persecution.

questions.question: What did her father say to her in his last moments, according to the research?
options: "Do not weep for me, for it is a joy"
"The parchments are burning and the letters are soaring in the air"
questions.explanation: The sentence separates the annihilation of the body from the eternity of the spirit, and became a compass in her life and her studies.

questions.question: True or false: The Sages of the Talmud granted Bruriah the title "the Tannait."
questions.explanation: Her words were always cited in the name of "the daughter of Rabbi Hananiah" or "the wife of Rabbi Meir," without an official title.

questions.question: True or false: According to tractate Pesachim, Bruriah learned three hundred traditions in one day.
questions.explanation: From three hundred rabbis. And yet, said Rabbi Yochanan, even she did not complete the "Book of Genealogies" (Sefer Yuchasin) in three years.

questions.question: What did Bruriah rule regarding the purification of a clay oven that had become impure?
options: Once they have moved it from its place
It becomes pure once they have stripped off its tunic, the outer layer of clay
Once they have immersed it in a mikveh
questions.explanation: Her brother said, "once they have moved it from its place." Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava ruled in accordance with her: "His daughter has spoken better than his son."

questions.question: Who said "Bruriah has spoken well" about her words concerning the klostra key?
questions.explanation: She distinguished between the key and the lock: "One detaches this key and hangs it on its fellow on the Sabbath," and therefore the key is a vessel in its own right.

questions.question: What was Bruriah's distinction regarding the verse "Let sins cease from the earth"?
options: It says "sins," the deeds, and not "sinners," the people
It says "from the earth" and not "from the city"
It is stated in the plural and not in the singular
The verse speaks of the Gentiles only
questions.explanation: When the sinners repent, "and the wicked will be no more": wickedness will vanish without destroying people.

questions.question: What happened when Rabbi Meir prayed for the ruffians, as Bruriah said?
questions.explanation: This is an approach of repair and rehabilitation, which prefers repentance to punishment.

questions.question: In which parable did Bruriah inform Rabbi Meir of the death of their sons?
options: A candle that went out on the Sabbath
A tree uprooted in a storm
A deposit whose owner came to take it
questions.explanation: When he answered that a deposit must be returned, she showed him the sons, and comforted him: "The Lord gave and the Lord has taken; blessed be the name of the Lord."

questions.question: Why did Bruriah wait until the end of the Sabbath to tell her husband?
options: Because she did not know until then
Because Rabbi Meir was on the road
To preserve the sanctity of the Sabbath and to spare him
questions.explanation: She laid the sons in a room and covered them, and waited until after Havdalah.

questions.question: True or false: Bruriah encouraged a student who studied in a whisper to continue studying that way.
questions.explanation: She kicked him and rebuked him: Torah is preserved only when it is said aloud, with all the limbs.

questions.question: From which verse did Bruriah justify the requirement to study aloud?
options: "And you shall meditate therein day and night"
"And you shall teach them diligently to your children"
questions.explanation: If the Torah is ordered in all 248 limbs, it is preserved. Study in a whisper leads to forgetting.

questions.question: To where did Rabbi Meir flee, according to tractate Avodah Zarah?
questions.explanation: The Gemara gives two reasons for the flight, one of which is "because of the Incident of Bruriah," without detail.

questions.question: True or false: The Gemara in Avodah Zarah specifies what the "Incident of Bruriah" is.
questions.explanation: The detail appears for the first time in the commentary attributed to Rashi on the passage, and many scholars doubt it.

questions.question: What did Rabbi Itam Henkin claim about the story in Rashi on the "Incident of Bruriah"?
options: That Rashi copied it from the Jerusalem Talmud
That Rabbi Meir himself told it
That it was not Rashi who wrote it, but a student who copied a corrupt note
That it is a proven historical truth
questions.explanation: He relies on the absence of the story from early manuscripts of Rashi. Other scholars see in it a story designed to deter women from study.

questions.question: Why, according to the research, were her words always cited in the name of her father or her husband?
options: Because her real name was not known
Because that was the custom with all the Tannaim
Because she herself asked for it
To confine her wisdom within the family structure and not make her an independent authority
questions.explanation: This expresses the tension between her scholarly superiority and the social structure of her generation.

questions.question: What two reasons does the Gemara give for Rabbi Meir's flight to Babylonia?
options: Persecution by the Romans after he rescued Bruriah's sister, and the "Incident of Bruriah"
A dispute with the Nasi, and a famine in the Land
The death of his sons, and the death of Bruriah
Decrees of religious persecution, and a debt to the Romans
questions.explanation: Rabbi Meir rescued Bruriah's sister from a Roman brothel, and as a result was pursued.

questions.question: How does Bruriah understand the process of learning, according to the research?
options: As full physical and vocal involvement, without which the Torah is forgotten
As listening to the teacher alone
As an orderly writing down of every tradition
questions.explanation: The Amora Shmuel also instructed his student to open his mouth while studying. A student of Rabbi Eliezer who studied in a whisper forgot his learning.
